subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 02, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 02, 2026

Hello AcreetionOS community,

As we continue to move forward with our mission to create a community-driven, user-friendly Linux distribution based on Arch Linux, we're excited to share some updates from the past week. Our team has been working hard to resolve conflicts and push out new features.

One of the key updates we've made is to resolve a geocode-glib update conflict that was affecting installed systems. This change ensures that our users can continue to rely on the stability and security of our distribution. Additionally, we've released a new kernel update, 7.2.15, which includes a handful of updates to improve performance and security.

In other news, we've seen a massive pile of security updates issued by AlmaLinux, addressing issues in .NET, aspell, bind, and other packages. We're committed to keeping our users safe and secure, and we're grateful for the work of the AlmaLinux team in identifying and addressing these vulnerabilities.

We've also seen some interesting articles and blog posts in the community, including a piece from the Hacktron blog on how a group was able to compromise the GNU Savannah forge and potentially push malicious code into the Bash shell. This serves as a reminder of the importance of security and the need for vigilance in our community.

On the development front, cobra3282000 has made several commits to the firefox-fix package, including restoring window position restore on Linux and fixing displaymanager job crash issues. Meanwhile, natalie has made an initial commit to acreetion-surf v2.0.0, which promises to bring exciting new features to our users.

We're also seeing progress on the Calamares configuration for Wayland, with cobra3282000 working on force-setting Wayland as the default desktop environment and installing lightdm-slick-greeter to fix displaymanager job crash issues. Additionally, cobra3282000 has made an initial commit to lmm-ai, a new project that aims to bring AI-powered features to our distribution.

We're grateful for the hard work and dedication of our community members, who are pushing the boundaries of what's possible with AcreetionOS. If you're interested in getting involved, we encourage you to join our Discord server and start contributing to the project.

As we move forward, we're committed to keeping our users informed and up-to-date on the latest developments. We'll continue to share updates and news from the community, and we invite you to join us on this journey.

Thanks for being part of the AcreetionOS community, and we look forward to seeing what the future holds for our distribution.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva
Co-Lead Developer, AcreetionOS
